# World index

Generated from `server/content` at `882699169a968e667d112006b714348bea4827ec`: 225 areas (63 top level), 22491 features, 3961 sites, 4536 npc spawn clusters, in [wiki/world.json](../world.json).

| Folder | Pages | One page per |
|---|---|---|
| [wiki/places/](../places/) | 225 | area: the sites whose deepest area it is, by kind, then each child area with its sites summed |
| [wiki/resources/](../resources/) | 91 | resource subtype (tree, rock, fishing spot, stall, thieving chest, pickpocket target): its dbrow data, then every site |
| [wiki/services/](../services/) | 15 | service kind (bank, shop, furnace, anvil, range, altar, ...): every site |
| [wiki/training/](../training/) | 6 | skill a curated method (wiki/world/methods.ts) trains: each method's floor XP/hr by level beside what the bots measured, and a README |

## What is generated

`wiki/world.json` and every page in `wiki/places/`, `wiki/resources/`, `wiki/services/` and `wiki/training/`
are written by `bun run world` (`wiki/world/build.ts`) from `server/content`, the curated areas and the curated
methods (`wiki/world/methods.ts`), and are committed with the code. Never edit them by hand: the next build
overwrites the edit, and `bun wiki/world/build.ts --check` (part of `bun run verify:conductor`) fails while a page
differs from a fresh build. The build also deletes pages it no longer renders from those four folders.

A site is a cluster of same-kind features (locs or npc spawns) in one area: its id is
`kind:area:n`, its centre the mean tile, its stand tile a walkable tile beside it. Coordinates are
`(x, z)`, with ` L<n>` above level 0; underground areas sit at z + 6400.

`npcSpawns` in world.json clusters every placed npc's spawns the same way, per config, whether or
not a feature kind takes it. The npc pages (`wiki/generate-npcs.ts`) read their Locations from it
and from the sites, and the shop pages (`wiki/generate-shops.ts`) their Coordinates from the shop
sites; both refuse a world.json built from other game data, so run `bun run world` first.

## Reach and requirements

A site's `reach` in world.json is what a walk from the Lumbridge spawn needs to get to its stand tile
(`wiki/world/reach.ts`, `reachGraph` then `fillReach`): its minimal requirement sets, `[[]]` for none and
`[]` when no walk gets there. An npc cluster's `reach` is that of the tiles beside it (`besideCluster` in
`place.ts`, with a wall check), because a bot talks to an npc from beside it. The fill keeps at most
`MAX_SETS` (16) sets per tile.

The pages show it in a Requires column: `-` for none, the sets joined with "or", `unreached`, or `no stand`
for a site with no stand tile; so a `-` row on a service or resource page is one a fresh account can walk to.
Within a set every requirement applies; any one set is enough. A set is written in the token forms of
`wiki/world/requirements.ts` (its header lists them):

| Token | Means |
|---|---|
| `quest:<id>`, `quest:<id>>=<stage>` | the quest is done; the quest has reached a stage (completion meets it) |
| `skill:<skill>:<level>`, `questpoints:<n>` | a base level; at least n quest points |
| `item:<obj>:worn\|held`, `category:<category>:worn\|held` | wearing or carrying the obj, or any obj of a category |
| `coins:<n>`, `consume:<obj>:<n>` | taken per crossing: a toll or fare, a pass or ticket |
| `members` | a members world |
| `loadout:<id>` | carrying none of a loadout rule's categories (Entrana: no weapons or armour) |
| `other:<text>` | a condition none of the forms fit; the build report lists each |

Sets are canonical (`canonicalSet`, `dominates`): a requirement another in the set implies is merged away
(`quest:x` covers `quest:x>=3`), the coins of every crossing on the way are summed into one `coins:<n>`, a
`consume` is summed per obj, and a set another set's requirements all imply is dropped. So a set that reads
`coins:10` has one toll on its way and `coins:20` two.

Resource and processor sites also carry `nearest` (`wiki/world/distance.ts`): the nearest bank, and for ore,
raw fish and smelted bars the nearest furnace, range or anvil, each as the sink site's id, the run ticks from the
site's stand tile to the sink's, and what that way needs, under the site's own `reach` sets. Distances are
run ticks only, because bots always run; a crossing (a stair, a gate, a ship, a cart, a sled) costs a fixed
`CROSSING_TICKS` for its kind, an estimate. The pages show it in a Nearest bank column (`none` when no bank is reached that way).

Where the ways come from: connectors (stairs, ladders, trapdoors, manholes, gangplanks) are read from
`scripts/ladders+stairs/` (`sources/connectors.ts`); gates from the scan of the scripts' door and gate triggers
(`sources/gate-scan.ts`), each confirmed or rejected in `gate-list.ts` (exported by `gates.ts`); transports
(ships, carts, sleds) from the sail scripts (`sources/transports.ts`) plus `CURATED_TRANSPORTS` in `gates.ts`.
Every curated entry cites its script, and the build fails on a candidate nobody reviewed.

### The unreached report

`bun run world` prints, after the build, a warning listing every site of a covered kind (bank, shop, resource,
service) that no walk from the Lumbridge spawn reaches: counted by kind, then by area, each with the tile it
looked from, its plane and the nearest reached tile on that plane. It is warnings only; `--check` leaves it
out. Work it as a curation to-do list: for each entry, read the scripts at the nearest reached tile, then
either add the missing connector, gate or transport (the derivation in `wiki/world/sources/`, or a row in
`gate-list.ts` / `gates.ts`), or say in the area's `notes` in `areas.ts` why it stays unreached, citing the
script. Known leftovers are the desert behind the Shantay Pass (a queued move), scripted moves outside
`ladders+stairs/` (the Mage Arena ladder, the Gnome Stronghold gate and railing, the lighthouse), and unnamed
underground areas.

## Methods

A method is a curated record in `wiki/world/methods.ts` (`MethodDef`): a family (the kind of action: woodcutting,
mining, fishing, pickpocket, stall, cooking; `model/families/`), a tile `at` in the gather site, the family's params,
a sink (`drop`, `bank`, or `process-bank`: a process step at a range, then the bank) and the promoted plans that run
it. Sites renumber when the data changes and tiles don't, so a record names a tile. `bun run world` resolves each
(`model/method.ts`: its site, sinks, legs, minimum level) into `methods[]` in world.json and fails naming a record it
can't; there is no rate grid in world.json.

The **floor** (`model/cycle.ts`) is the tick-perfect rate of a method at a profile (levels, tool, food): the game's
formulas (`model/`, each citing its script) for ideal play over the shortest way, with no tick wasted and banking at
its minimum tick cost. Legs are run ticks. A bot measures at or below it, and the gap is what a tick-perfect pass
works on; a measured figure above its floor is a model bug. The pages in `wiki/training/` show the floor by level
beside the measured figures; `methodRate(id, profile)` and `bestMethods(skill, profile, { met, maxWilderness,
multiway })` in `query.ts` give it to code, `bestMethods` ranked by floor XP/hr.

Measured figures are curated, not read at build time: when a goal finishes, `bun conductor/tools/stats.ts <bot>
--methods` prints the paste-ready `measured` entry (XP/hr, the levels and tool the runs started at, bot, date, hours,
the command), and the conductor pastes it into the record. A plan names its method (`PlanDef.method`, see
`conductor/docs/plans.md`) and the record lists the plan back.

Adding a method:

1. Write the record in `methods.ts`: a tile in the site, the params, the sink, the plans.
2. A new kind of action needs a family module in `model/families/` (one file, its registry line in `index.ts`) with a
   test worked by hand from its script in `test/families.test.ts`.
3. `bun run world`; read the method's row in `wiki/training/<skill>.md`.
4. After bots have run it, paste the `stats.ts --methods` entry into `measured`.

## Where corrections go

| Wrong on a page | Fix it in |
|---|---|
| An area's name, extent, parent or notes; a site named after the wrong place | `wiki/world/areas.ts` |
| A loc or npc missing, or listed as the wrong kind or subtype | the rule table in `wiki/world/classify.ts` |
| Sites split or merged wrongly, or a bad stand tile | `wiki/world/place.ts` (`SITE_RADIUS`, the stand rules) |
| A page's layout or wording | `wiki/world/render/` |
| A door or gate and what it needs; a Requires cell, or a site reading unreached that a bot gets to | its row in `wiki/world/gate-list.ts` (exported by `gates.ts`), or the derivation in `wiki/world/sources/gate-scan.ts`; else an area note in `areas.ts` saying why |
| A transport (ship, cart, sled) or its fare | `CURATED_TRANSPORTS` in `wiki/world/gates.ts`, or `wiki/world/sources/transports.ts` |
| A staircase, ladder or trapdoor missing, or with the wrong landing | `wiki/world/sources/connectors.ts` (the scripts give landings; there is no table to patch) |
| A connector's name or hazard note, or a connector the conductor's walker leaves out | `OVERRIDES` and `LEFT_OUT` in `conductor/lib/connectors.ts` (the rows themselves are generated from world.json) |
| A method's tile, params, sink, plans or a measured figure | its record in `wiki/world/methods.ts`, then `bun run world` |
| A method's floor (a formula, a cycle or tool rule) | the family module in `wiki/world/model/families/`, or `model/` (`cycle.ts`, `rate.ts`, `roll.ts`), with its hand-worked test |

Then run `bun run world` and commit the code with the regenerated files. What is learned in game
about a place (a hazard, a route, a rate measured) goes in `learnings/` per the `knowledge` skill,
naming the page.
